purpose: Provides practical category buckets and keyword mappings for normalizing transaction activity in weekly cash-flow reviews.
normalization_principles: Use practical owner-friendly buckets instead of overly technical accounting categories.
Preserve uncertainty when a transaction cannot be classified confidently.
Do not treat transfers as operating revenue or operating expense without confirmation.
Do not silently delete or ignore duplicate-looking transactions.
Prefer clear assumptions over false precision.
Use existing CSV categories when they appear reliable, but normalize them when they are too granular or inconsistent.

category_buckets.description: Customer payments, sales deposits, invoice payments, platform payouts, and other operating receipts.
category_buckets.notes: Do not automatically classify all deposits as revenue. Transfers, owner contributions, refunds, and loan proceeds should be separated when visible.

category_buckets.description: Employee payroll, wages, payroll taxes, and payroll provider debits.
category_buckets.notes: Payroll pressure may become a watch item when large relative to inflows or upcoming obligations.

category_buckets.description: Payments to freelancers, 1099 workers, agencies, contractors, or consultants.
category_buckets.notes: Some consultant payments may also fit Professional Services. Use description context.

category_buckets.description: Rent, lease, utilities, office, coworking, and facility costs.
category_buckets.notes: Rent or facility obligations may be watch items if upcoming or unusually large.

category_buckets.description: SaaS tools, subscriptions, cloud software, productivity tools, and recurring app costs.
category_buckets.notes: Small recurring charges can stack up. Flag high subscription volume as Low Risk or Watch List depending on amount.

category_buckets.description: Ad spend, marketing services, lead generation, SEO, sponsorship, and campaign costs.
category_buckets.notes: Marketing should be reviewed when cash is tightening or spend spikes.

category_buckets.description: Loan payments, financing payments, line of credit payments, MCA/advance repayments, interest, or principal payments.
category_buckets.notes: Do not recommend stopping payments or refinancing. Heavy or frequent debt service can be a High Attention watch item.

category_buckets.description: Federal, state, local, payroll, sales, and estimated tax payments.
category_buckets.notes: Do not provide tax advice. Suggest verifying obligations with a qualified professional.

category_buckets.description: Inventory, materials, supplies, wholesale purchases, product costs, and cost of goods sold.
category_buckets.notes: Inventory spikes may be normal for product businesses but should be explained if material.

category_buckets.description: Legal, accounting, bookkeeping, consulting, advisory, compliance, and professional support costs.
category_buckets.notes: Do not treat professional service spend as bad by default. Flag only if unusually large or relevant to cash pressure.

category_buckets.description: Business insurance, liability insurance, workers comp, auto, health, or policy premiums.
category_buckets.notes: Large annual or quarterly premiums may distort a weekly view.

category_buckets.description: Travel, lodging, transportation, meals, parking, fuel, and related operating expenses.
category_buckets.notes: Do not provide tax deductibility guidance.

category_buckets.description: Owner withdrawals, member draws, shareholder distributions, and related owner cash movement.
category_buckets.notes: Owner draws may be sensitive. Describe neutrally and avoid judgment.

category_buckets.description: Internal transfers, account-to-account movement, wires, Zelle transfers, and bank transfers.
category_buckets.notes: Transfers should not be treated as operating revenue or operating expense without confirmation.

category_buckets.description: Refunds, reversals, chargebacks, returned payments, and corrections.
category_buckets.notes: Direction depends on context. Flag unclear refunds, reversals, and chargebacks.

category_buckets.description: Bank fees, service charges, overdraft fees, wire fees, and account fees.
category_buckets.notes: Repeated overdraft or NSF fees may be a watch item.

category_buckets.description: Transactions that cannot be confidently classified.
category_buckets.notes: Use this category when classification is unclear. Explain assumptions in the Data Quality Check.

matching_rules: Use description, memo, vendor, customer, category, and transaction type fields as classification clues.
If multiple categories match, choose the category most supported by transaction direction and description context.
If transaction direction conflicts with category, preserve uncertainty and flag it.
If the transaction appears to be a transfer, prioritize Transfers over Revenue / Inflows or expense categories.
If the transaction appears to be a refund, reversal, or chargeback, prioritize Refunds / Reversals / Chargebacks and explain uncertainty.
If category confidence is low, use Other / Uncategorized.

confidence_levels.meaning: Column names, direction, description, and category all support the classification.
Most evidence supports the classification, but one field is missing or vague.
Classification is based on limited clues and should be reviewed.
The transaction should remain uncategorized or be flagged for user confirmation.

do_not_do: Do not classify every deposit as revenue.
Do not classify every outgoing transfer as an expense.
Do not ignore owner draws or distributions if visible.
Do not treat loan proceeds as operating revenue.
Do not provide tax deductibility guidance.
Do not make lending, underwriting, accounting, legal, tax, or investment recommendations.
